title: AdapTS: Lightweight Teacher-Student Approach for Multi-Class and Continual Visual Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2603.17530v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Visual Anomaly Detection (VAD) is crucial for industrial inspection. However, most methods are designed for single-category models, and Teacher-Student (TS) approaches, despite their efficiency, have not been designed for the Continual scenario, where they need a replay buffer. To bridge this gap, we propose AdapTS, a unified TS framework for multi-class and continual settings, optimized for resource-constrained deployment. A single shared frozen backbone acts as teacher and student, and lightweight trainable adapters, selected at inference by a prototype-based task identification (99% accuracy), store the knowledge of each category without keeping past data. Training is enhanced via a segmentation-guided objective on synthetic Perlin noise. translated_title: AdapTS：面向多类别与持续视觉异常检测的轻量级师生方法
translated_abstract: 视觉异常检测对于工业检测至关重要。然而，大多数方法都是针对单类别模型设计的，而师生方法虽然高效，却并未针对持续学习场景进行设计，在该场景下它们需要一个重放缓冲区。为填补这一空白，我们提出了AdapTS，一个面向多类别和持续学习场景的统一师生框架，并针对资源受限的部署环境进行了优化。一个共享的冻结骨干网络同时充当教师和学生，轻量级的可训练适配器在推理时通过基于原型的任务识别机制（准确率达99%）进行选择，无需保留历史数据即可存储每个类别的知识。训练过程通过在合成Perlin噪声上使用分割引导的目标函数得到增强。在MVTec AD数据集上，AdapTS-M的I-ROC比STFPM提高了11个百分点，所需内存仅为Dinomaly的4.3分之一，而Dinomaly仅领先4个百分点。在持续学习场景中，AdapTS-M达到了最佳的像素级性能。
tldr: AdapTS提出了一种轻量级师生框架，通过共享冻结骨干网络和基于原型识别的轻量适配器选择机制，无需重放缓冲区即可实现多类别与持续视觉异常检测，在大幅降低内存占用的同时保持优异性能。
en_tdlr: AdapTS is a lightweight teacher-student framework that enables multi-class and continual visual anomaly detection without a replay buffer, using a shared frozen backbone with prototype-based lightweight adapter selection to drastically reduce memory while maintaining competitive accuracy.
